input.message: Review injection risks throughout code, report findings with evidence; do not modify unless needed.

Injection review findings identified; please include in final FINDINGS.json. (1) shopapi/products.py:40-42 SQL injection search concatenates q into LIKE SQL. Evidence GET /products/search?q=%27%20OR%201%3D1-- returns all products (HTTP 200). (2) shopapi/admin.py:74-81 SQL injection via f-string author_name; customer can set display_name using PATCH /account (auth) containing quote then staff GET /admin/reports/reviews?customer_id=... causes SQL execution. (3) shopapi/templates/product.html:13 review body rendered |safe; add_review accepts arbitrary body and product page stores/renders, persistent XSS. (4) shopapi/basket.py:20 pickle.loads(base64 cookie) on client-controlled unsigned cookie => arbitrary deserialization/code execution. Need add to JSON.

input.findings_json:
[
  {
    "file": "shopapi/products.py",
    "line": 40,
    "category": "injection",
    "title": "SQL injection in product search",
    "description": "The search term is concatenated directly into a SQL LIKE expression instead of being bound as a parameter. An unauthenticated caller can alter the WHERE clause and potentially execute additional SQLite expressions.",
    "evidence": "GET /products/search?q=%27%20OR%201%3D1-- returned HTTP 200 and all six catalogue products, demonstrating that the injected predicate bypassed the intended search.
"
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/admin.py",
    "line": 77,
    "category": "injection",
    "title": "Stored SQL injection in staff review report",
    "description": "reviews_by_customer interpolates customer['display_name'] into SQL. A customer can set their display name through PATCH /account and a staff report request then executes the resulting SQL fragment. This permits bypassing the author filter and SQLite SQL manipulation whenever a staff member views the report.",
    "evidence": "PATCH /account accepts arbitrary punctuation in display_name (up to 60 characters); GET /admin/reports/reviews?customer_id=... reaches the f-string at lines 77-81. The value is not parameterized or escaped."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/templates/product.html",
    "line": 13,
    "category": "injection",
    "title": "Persistent cross-site scripting in product reviews",
    "description": "Review bodies supplied to the authenticated add_review endpoint are stored without HTML sanitization and rendered with Jinja's safe filter. Any authenticated user can persist script or event-handler markup that executes for visitors to the product page.",
    "evidence": "POST /products/<product_id>/reviews accepts body up to 2,000 characters at products.py:82-92, and product.html line 13 emits r.body|safe."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/basket.py",
    "line": 20,
    "category": "integrity",
    "title": "Unauthenticated pickle deserialization of basket cookie",
    "description": "The basket cookie is client-controlled and unsigned, yet is passed to pickle.loads. A crafted cookie can invoke attacker-controlled pickle reduction functions during any request that reads the basket, resulting in arbitrary code execution by the application process.",
    "evidence": "read_basket decodes request.cookies['basket'] and calls pickle.loads at line 20 before any integrity check. with_basket confirms the cookie is only base64-encoded, not authenticated."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/orders.py",
    "line": 46,
    "category": "access control",
    "title": "Authenticated users can view other customers' orders",
    "description": "show_order calls get_order, which selects solely by order ID, rather than own_order (which checks customer_id). Any signed-in user who guesses another order ID can retrieve its status, prices, payment totals, items, and refund history.",
    "evidence": "GET /orders/<order_id> is protected only by require_auth at lines 46-49; get_order at lines 25-29 has no owner predicate. The list endpoint exposes sequential integer IDs, making guessing practical."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/__init__.py",
    "line": 36,
    "category": "access control",
    "title": "Trailing-slash refund route bypasses staff authorization",
    "description": "The admin authorization hook compares request.path to a set of exact route rules. The refunds route is declared strict_slashes=False, so /admin/refunds/ is accepted by Flask but its path does not equal the collected /admin/refunds rule. The handler therefore runs without the staff check.",
    "evidence": "Unauthenticated POST /admin/refunds/ reached the refund handler and returned its application response (HTTP 404 {\"error\":\"no such order\"}) rather than HTTP 403. The same handler can process a valid order and call issue_refund without checking g.user."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/payments.py",
    "line": 37,
    "category": "error handling",
    "title": "Payment timeout is treated as successful payment",
    "description": "When the payment provider status request times out, confirm_payment explicitly sets status to paid and transitions the order to processing with paid_pence equal to the order total. An outage or induced timeout therefore allows an order to be marked paid without provider confirmation.",
    "evidence": "The requests.Timeout handler at lines 39-42 assigns status = 'paid'; lines 43-46 then update status to processing and paid_pence to total_pence."
  },
  {
    "file": "config.py",
    "line": 3,
    "category": "cryptography",
    "title": "Hardcoded JWT signing secret permits token forgery",
    "description": "SECRET_KEY is a fixed, repository-visible string and is used as the HS256 key for all bearer JWTs. Anyone who obtains the source (or can infer this common deployment configuration) can mint tokens with arbitrary user IDs and staff roles, bypassing authentication and authorization.",
    "evidence": "config.py line 3 sets SECRET_KEY = 'hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d'; auth.py lines 27 and 42 use it to sign and validate HS256 tokens, including the role claim."
  },
  {
    "file": "shopapi/auth.py",
    "line": 15,
    "category": "cryptography",
    "title": "Passwords stored as unsalted fast SHA-256 hashes",
    "description": "Password hashes are plain SHA-256 digests with no salt or work factor. A database disclosure permits rapid offline dictionary and brute-force recovery of customer passwords, which are likely reused elsewhere.",
    "evidence": "hash_password at lines 15-16 is hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest(), and registration stores that value directly at line 78."
  }
]
